name: MonarchAiTypingDots
title: AiTypingDots
summary: Three dots that rise and brighten in turn to show the assistant is writing, for places with no room for a label.
whenToUse: In a chat dock, a conversation row or a small message bubble that waits for the first words of a reply.
whenNotToUse: Where there is room for text, say what is happening in words. For a wait that is not the assistant writing, use the standard ProgressView (see spinner).
api: MonarchAiTypingDots.init(label: String? = nil, size: MonarchAiTypingDotsSize = .md, isAnnounced: Bool = true)

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken label "Assistant is typing".

options.name: size
options.description: sm: 4-point dots for docks and dense rows. md: 6-point dots for a message bubble.

options.name: isAnnounced
options.description: Whether the label is announced when the dots appear. Pass false when something else already announces the state.

states.name: animating
states.description: Each dot rises by 0.6 of its size and goes from 40% to full opacity, one after another, in a 1.2-second cycle.

states.name: Reduce Motion
states.description: The dots are still, at 70% opacity.

appearance: The dots use the assistant (ai) strong colour role in every theme, which the high-contrast themes resolve to a stronger colour.
platformNotes: The timing follows the web: a cycle of 0.75 of the shimmer duration and 0.125 of it between dots. The web eases between keyframes with its standard curve; iOS uses a smooth step, so the motion is close but not identical. The web also stops the animation in forced-colours mode, which iOS does not have; the high-contrast themes keep the animation.
accessibility: The dots are one element whose label is the label parameter or "Assistant is typing".
When the dots appear and isAnnounced is true, the label is posted as a VoiceOver announcement.
With Reduce Motion on the dots do not move or change opacity.
The dots scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: The announcement is posted every time the view appears, so remove and insert it once per reply, not per token.
A rising dot draws slightly above the view's bounds, as on the web; leave the default spacing around it.

examples.title: In a conversation row, announced elsewhere
